KIT design language

Source: vignettes/articles/design-language.Rmd
design-language.Rmd

This page is brand/en/design-language.md in kitDesign (the English translation of brand/KIT設計語言.md, which is the source of truth). To see what the components look like, see Components.

Easy to see, safe to click, results first.

The design language shared by the KIT research tools (kitJoin, kitsUI, and future Shiny apps). New apps follow this document, so once people learn one tool, they can use the others.

  • Companions:
    • Implementation: the R package kitDesign (kit_page(), components, modules, the CSS in inst/www/). This document lives in kitDesign’s brand/, and this copy is the source of truth.
    • Design system (live samples, tokens, logo): https://claude.ai/artifact/GFN5Q5ie9jAHKwmsBaxb2M (private; visible only when shared)
    • _brand.yml: design variables such as colors and fonts; logo/: the logo (SVG, PNG)
    • What every component looks like: kitDesign::kit_gallery()
  • Status: v1.1 (2026-10-31). v1.0 merged v0.2’s “additions after design review” into the main text; v1.1 adds kitDesign 0.2.0’s charts (kit_plotly_style()), the danger button, the heatmap color scale, the step card rule “choose first, refine later”, and “Author’s decisions” 6–9. Where the spec and the code differ, this document follows the code; the differences are listed in the last section.

Who we design for

Who Researchers and research assistants, mostly aged 40–60; they use SPSS and Excel, and may not write R
How often A few times a year, an hour or two each time; every return feels like the first time
Doing what Working with real research data: joining, converting, calibrating, scoring. Wrong results end up in papers
Where Desktops or laptops in the office, 13–27 inch screens; sometimes a phone to check results
Biggest fears Not knowing what to click next; clicking and not knowing whether it worked; results that look right but are wrong

Priority: correct > clear > good-looking. Looking good makes people willing to use the tool and comfortable reading it, but it must never cost the first two. Keep the design simple and clean.

Seven principles

  1. One lead per page. Each page has exactly one primary button (nb-lime), for example “開始校準” (“Start calibration”). Everything else is supporting cast and steps back visually.
  2. Results first, details later. After a click, the first thing people see is the status box: a one-sentence conclusion, two or three key points, and one table or one chart. Parameter tables, logs, check tables, and R code go in the details row, opened on demand.
  3. Problems must be seen. The most dangerous case is “looks successful but is actually wrong”. If anything needs attention, the status cannot be a plain 【完成】 (“Done”). Actions that change results (skipping a scale, treating codes as missing values) are clicked by the user, never done automatically.
  4. A frame is a unit. Anything with a black frame is either something you can operate or a complete unit (a button, an input, one result, one chart). No frames inside frames, and no decorative frames.
  5. Quiet supporting cast. Explanations, hints, and technical details use the hint size and text-hint color, no frame, and are collapsed by default. First-time users can find them; experienced users are not slowed down.
  6. Every page looks the same. The same page skeleton, the same components, the same wording. Learn one page and you can use the others; learn kitJoin and you can use kitsUI.
  7. Plain language first. The main screen uses short sentences in the Chinese commonly used in Taiwan. English terms (function names, column names) go in the details or in downloaded files.

Visual foundations

Style: restrained neo-brutalism

We keep three traits: black frames, offset shadows with zero blur, and flat color blocks with black text. Everything is toned down for middle-aged users and long reading sessions:

Typical neo-brutalism The KIT way Why
3–5px frames bw-frame 2px Matches the stroke weight of the rounded typeface; easy on the eyes over time
6–8px shadows shadow-header 4px, shadow-card 3px, shadow-sm 2px Shadows only mean “clickable” or “a result”
Large areas of saturated color Saturated color only on the header, the primary button, and the current step Large bright areas are tiring over time
Deliberate misalignment Aligned, regular spacing A tool should be predictable

Color

Colors are defined by role, and each role has exactly one color.

  • Background: the whole page is nb-page (off-white); cards, inputs, tables, and charts use nb-card. Light only; there is no dark mode.
  • Ink: all text, frames, and shadows are nb-ink. Text on color blocks is always nb-ink, never white. The only white text is the black header row of the main data table.
  • Lead: nb-lime is used only for the header, the primary button, the current tab, the current step number, and the selected item in a dropdown. Never use it as a text color.
  • Brand and links: nb-green (the same color as the logo’s dark green) is for links, progress bars, ✓, and checkboxes. On hover, nb-green-hover. Never use it as a large background.
  • Four semantic colors; seeing the color tells you the meaning:
    • nb-mint done
    • nb-yellow needs attention (also used for 【要重新執行】 (“Run again”))
    • nb-salmon stopped (also used for the danger button)
    • nb-sky information
  • Color must never be the only signal. The status box always has a text label: 【完成】 (“Done”), 【完成，但請注意】 (“Done, but note”), 【停下來】 (“Stopped”), 【要重新執行】 (“Run again”); the ✓ on tabs and the ! in checklists both carry hidden text.
  • These are the only grays:
    • Supporting text text-hint
    • Disabled text text-disabled
    • Lines line, line-soft
    • Disabled frames border-disabled
  • Emphasis text: “還差：…” (“Still needed: …”) uses text-todo; the checklist ! uses text-decide; a single problem in a list uses text-stop.
  • Logo colors (logo-bean, logo-leaf) are only for the logo and illustrations, never for the interface.
  • Charts: categorical colors use the colorblind-friendly Okabe–Ito palette, taken in order: chart-blue, chart-orange, chart-green, chart-purple, chart-sky, chart-vermillion. Reference lines and bands use chart-neutral; continuous values use chart-sequential.

Typography

  • One rounded typeface throughout: Chiron GoRound TC (sans, Google Fonts, weights 400, 700, 900).
    • Hierarchy comes from weight and size, not from switching typefaces.
    • Use weights 400 and 700; the header h1 may go to 900. Secondary buttons and “no problem” checklist items use 500.
  • Code, raw messages, and values in diagrams: JetBrains Mono (mono), falling back to the rounded typeface for Chinese. Ligatures are always off (font-variant-ligatures: none), so <- and |> display as typed.
  • Six type sizes, base 17px (html { font-size: 17px }):
    • display: header h1
    • h4: section titles
    • h5: subtitles, step card titles, the primary button, the first line of the status box
    • body: body text
    • small: tables, step summaries
    • hint: hints, collapsible titles, group labels, the version line
  • The smallest size is hint (about 14px); anything smaller is for chart tick labels only.
  • Put a half-width space between Chinese and English or numbers: 「688 人」, 「依 SPSS 數值標籤」. Numbers of four digits or more get thousands separators: 「3,389 人」.

Frames, shadows, corners

  • Frames:
    • Top-level components use bw-frame (2px) nb-ink.
    • Table row dividers and secondary buttons use bw-line (1.5px).
    • Diagram grid lines use bw-hair (1px).
  • Corners: everything radius (8px); progress bars radius-bar; step numbers radius-round.
  • Shadows, from largest to smallest:
    • shadow-header: the header only.
    • shadow-card: results, including the status box, charts, the current step card, and the primary button.
    • shadow-sm: clickable things, including tabs, regular buttons, dropdowns, and focused inputs.
    • No shadow: callouts, code, inputs (when not focused), finished or not-yet-available step cards, tables, secondary buttons. A callout is not a result, so it has no shadow; that keeps the status box always the most prominent box on the page.
  • Interaction:
    • On hover, move 1px down and to the right; the shadow becomes shadow-hover.
    • On press, move all the way and drop the shadow; animation 80ms.
    • The current tab looks “pressed”: lime, no shadow, offset 2px.
    • When the user has set “reduce motion”, no offset and no animation.
  • Keyboard focus: 3px focus outline, offset 3px outward. Tabs, file buttons, and checkboxes all need it.

Spacing and layout

  • Spacing uses a 0.25rem unit, from sp-1 (0.25rem) to sp-5 (2.4rem).
    • Between sections: sp-5.
    • Between components in the same section: sp-3.
    • Between buttons in a row: sp-2.
  • Content is at most content-max (1140px) wide, centered; gutter on the left and right, 1rem at ≤ bp-tablet.
  • When settings and results sit side by side: settings on the left 1/3, results on the right 2/3; at ≤ bp-tablet they stack, settings on top.
  • Tables are as wide as their content, not stretched; at most the layout width, and they scroll sideways inside their own frame when wider.

Icons

  • Text symbols only:
    • ✓: done, no problem
    • !: needs a decision
    • i: reminder
    • →: next step, leaves this page
    • ▸／▾: collapse
    • ↑↓: sort
    • ⬇: download
    • ①–④: only for tabs of an ordered workflow
  • No emoji and no other icon fonts.
  • Icons always come with text; symbols next to text get aria-hidden="true".
  • Each symbol has exactly one meaning.

Logo

  • The header uses the full logo kit-logo (bean + KIT wordmark), 5.6rem tall; 3.6rem on phones. The browser tab icon uses only the bean, kit-mark.
  • Leave clear space of at least 1/4 of the logo height on all sides. It may sit on nb-lime, nb-page, or nb-card; not on status colors or nb-green.
  • Do not change its colors or proportions, and do not add frames or shadows. Use alt="" when the tool name is already next to it.

Components

Each component lists its purpose, R function, appearance, rules, and don’ts. Live samples are on the design system’s components page.

Header

The header tells users which tool this is and which version; an app has exactly one, at the very top.

  • R: kit_header() (kit_theme.R), reads Version and Date from DESCRIPTION.
  • Appearance:
    • nb-lime block, bw-frame frame, shadow-header.
    • Full logo on the left (5.6rem tall); on the right the tool name (display), one line of tagline (bold), and one line of version (hint).
  • You provide: the tool name (“KIT ×× 工具”, “KIT ×× tool”) and the tagline (database name · what this tool does).
  • Rules:
    • The version line is always there; it is needed when reporting problems.
    • Do not change the tool name when testing with other data.
    • Phones (≤ 576px): logo 3.6rem, h1 1.35rem.
  • Don’t: put buttons or navigation in the header; change the logo’s colors or proportions, or put a frame around it.

Step tabs (NavTabs)

Step tabs are the main navigation inside a tool: a row of clickable blocks; the current one is lime, finished ones get a ✓, and not-yet-available ones are gray.

  • Two kinds:
    • Ordered workflow (kitsUI): ① 資料 → ② 題目校準 → ③ 連結 → ④ 受試者評分 (① Data → ② Item calibration → ③ Linking → ④ Respondent scoring), with circled numbers.
    • Not every page is required (kitJoin): three groups, unnumbered, each with a hint group label above it:
      • 準備 (Prepare)
      • 做出資料（選一個） (Make the data (pick one))
      • 其他工具 (Other tools)
  • R: kitsUI uses navset_tab plus the states from kit_tabs_js(); kitJoin draws the tab bar with kit_navgroups(), and the real tabs are a tabsetPanel(type = "hidden"), so updateTabsetPanel() works as usual.
  • Appearance:
    • White background, bw-frame frame, shadow-sm.
    • Current tab nb-lime, no shadow, moved 2px down and to the right (the pressed look).
    • Standalone small tools and “使用手冊” (“User guide”): dashed frame, no shadow, placed at the far right.
  • States:
    • Done: ✓ (nb-green), plus hidden text 「（已完成）」 (“(done)”).
    • Not yet available: bg-disabled background, text-disabled text; on hover, explains what must be done first.
    • Needs re-running: the ✓ is removed.
  • Rules:
    • Tab names are “noun + verb”: 檔案上傳 (file upload), 遺漏值處理 (missing value handling).
    • At ≤ 768px the tabs stay in one row and scroll sideways; they do not wrap.
  • Don’t: wrap the tabs in another big frame; use numbers that imply every step is required when the steps are actually alternatives.

Page guide (“What this page does”) (PageGuide)

“這一頁做什麼” (“What this page does”) is a one-line explanation at the top of each tab, collapsed by default; first-time users open it to see the steps.

  • R: kit_tab_guide(goal, steps, output, technical = NULL, note = NULL, diagram = NULL).
  • Appearance:
    • No frame, hint size, text-hint color, with a faint line rule below.
    • “看步驟 ▸” (“See steps ▸”) is underlined nb-green text.
  • You provide:
    • goal: one sentence, at most 30 characters.
    • steps: 3–6 points.
    • output: what you get.
    • Optional: note for extra notes, technical (one more collapsed level), diagram (see Diagram).
  • Don’t: open it by default; put settings or buttons inside it; make it a card.

Button

There are four kinds of buttons, and each page has only one primary button; labels start with a verb and say clearly what happens on click.

  • R: kit_button(id, label, kind = "secondary"), where kind is "primary", "secondary", or "danger"; a regular button is just the default look of shiny::actionButton().
  • Primary button (btn-primary):
    • nb-lime background, h5 size, shadow-card, height ≥ 48px.
    • One per page, plus the “下一步” (“Next step”) at the bottom.
  • Regular button (actionButton() default): white background, bw-frame frame, shadow-sm, height ≥ 40px. Used for in-flow buttons such as “對，下一步” (“Yes, next step”).
  • Secondary button (kind = "secondary", btn-sm btn-outline-secondary):
    • White background, bw-line frame, no shadow, 0.85rem, weight 500, height ≥ 36px.
    • Used for download, select all, example files, move up/down, copy.
  • Danger button (kind = "danger", btn-sm btn-danger):
    • nb-salmon background, nb-ink text, bw-line frame, same size as the secondary button; stays nb-salmon on hover and press.
    • When disabled it uses the disabled look (bg-disabled background), not salmon.
    • Used for delete, remove, and “這一回合不做” (“Skip this round”).
  • Disabled: bg-disabled background, text-hint text, border-disabled frame, no shadow; do not use opacity. A disabled primary button always has a “還差：…” (“Still needed: …”) line above it (see ReadyLine).
  • Rules:
    • Buttons or links that leave the page end with “→”.
    • The recommended option goes first and says 「（建議）」 (“(recommended)”).
    • When a download is the lead of the page (for example, a response file), use kit-download btn-primary.
  • Don’t: write 「確定」 (“OK”) or 「送出」 (“Submit”); put two lime buttons on one page; use white text.

Download button (DownloadButton)

The download button looks the same as a secondary button (⬇ icon + 「下載 CSV」, “Download CSV”), but the file name is saved correctly in every browser, Chinese names included.

  • R: kit_download_button(session, id, label, filename, content, class = NULL), placed inside renderUI(); in tests, click download with kit_test_download(session, id).
  • Appearance: <a class="btn btn-default kit-download">, styled as a secondary button; add class = "btn-primary" when it is the lead of the page.
  • Rules:
    • The file name is decided when the button is drawn; the last segment of the URL, Content-Disposition (filename and the UTF-8 filename*), and the download attribute all use the same file name.
    • The file is written only when download is clicked; if it cannot be written, a red notification appears (it does not disappear on its own) with the plain-language message from kit_abort() as is.
    • .csv, .zip, and .html use their own MIME types; everything else (.sav, .csv.gz) is application/octet-stream, so the browser does not add an extra extension.
    • The app sets options(kitDesign.app = "kitJoin") once in .onLoad(): it tells the log which app wrote it; when a file name is all Chinese, the ASCII fallback name for older browsers is the lowercase app name (「第一波.sav」 → 「kitjoin.sav」).
  • Don’t: use shiny::downloadHandler() (Chinese file names become missing-download_sav in some browsers).

Input

Inputs are white with a black frame, the label above and a small hint below; the default value is the most common and safest one.

  • R: Shiny’s own selectInput(), textInput(), radioButtons(), checkboxInput(); hints use .kit-hint.
  • Appearance:
    • White background, bw-frame frame, radius.
    • shadow-sm appears on focus; when a dropdown is open, the selected item is nb-lime.
    • Checkboxes and radio buttons are always 20px, nb-green when selected.
  • Rules:
    • 2–5 options: radio buttons, so all are visible at once; more than 5: a dropdown.
    • For required fields, write 「（必填）」 (“(required)”); no red asterisks.
    • Advanced options go under 「進階設定 ▸」 (“Advanced settings ▸”) (see Details).
    • Values guessed from column names get the pale yellow bg-guess background, reminding users to check them.
    • One field, two uses: for the same column, some files need “pick a column in the file” and others need “the same value for every row” (cohort TDCYP, wave 2009). Use one dropdown you can type into; do not add a separate mode choice.
    • A group of checkboxes needs a group name; more than 8 in a row becomes a table or gets “select all”.
  • Don’t: give inputs a shadow (except on focus); put dropdowns in a table without an aria-label.

Status box (StatusBox)

The status box is the first thing to look at after clicking the primary button: four fixed labels, colors, and wordings.

  • R: kit_status(), kit_done_status() (switches to needs-attention automatically when there are warnings), kit_error_status(e, action, todo), kit_stale_status(run_label); rendered with make_status_ui().
  • Four states:
State Label Background
Done 【完成】 (“Done”) nb-mint
Needs attention 【完成，但請注意】 (“Done, but note”) nb-yellow
Stopped 【停下來】 (“Stopped”) nb-salmon
Needs redoing 【要重新執行】 (“Run again”) nb-yellow
  • Appearance: bw-frame frame, shadow-card; the most prominent box on the page.
  • Content:
    • First line: label + one-sentence conclusion, bold, about h5 size. For example 「【完成】串接完成：結果共 3,389 列 × 2,058 欄。」 (“[Done] Join complete: 3,389 rows × 2,058 columns.”)
    • Then: at most 3 points, things needing attention first, key results after; the rest go under 「還有 N 點」 (“N more”).
    • When stopped: always say what to do, with a button or link; R’s original message goes under 「原始訊息」 (“Original message”).
  • Rules:
    • After a run, scroll the status box to the top of the screen (kit_scroll_to()).
    • The key output below the status box is one table or one chart; do not add another “result summary” box.
  • Don’t: invent new labels; put the raw error message at the top level.

Callout

A callout is a reminder you should know before clicking; it is not a result, so it has no shadow.

  • R: kit_callout(..., warn = FALSE). Cloud-version reminders look the same: the banner below the header kit_cloud_banner(), and the usage notes at the very bottom of the page kit_cloud_footer(sections, links) (small gray text; the wording comes from the app); check whether it is the cloud version with kit_is_cloud().
  • Two kinds:
    • Information (nb-sky): general extra notes, for example 「外部連結不適用：……這不是錯誤」 (“External linking does not apply: … this is not an error”).
    • Attention (warn = TRUE, nb-yellow): for example 「資料裡有疑似遺漏值代碼，建議先到遺漏值處理」 (“The data contain what look like missing-value codes; we suggest going to missing value handling first”).
  • Appearance: bw-frame frame, no shadow; links inside are bold nb-ink.
  • Rules:
    • At most one callout per block.
    • If it can go in the status box, do not open a separate callout.
    • When there is a button, put it outside the frame.
  • Don’t: use a callout to report results; put a frame inside the frame.

Data table (DataTable)

The data table is one of the leads of the results: white background, black header row, width follows content; long tables show only the first rows.

  • R: kit_static_table(df) (integers get thousands separators automatically), kit_preview_table(df, priority_cols, n), kit_rows_note(nrow, ncol, shown_rows).
  • Appearance:
    • White background, bw-frame outer frame, nb-ink header row with white text.
    • Thin bw-line lines between rows, bg-stripe zebra stripes, small size.
    • Numbers right-aligned, tabular figures.
  • Rules:
    • An h4 title above, plus one hint line: 「共 157 列，以下前 20 列。」 (“157 rows; the first 20 are shown below.”). The full table is downloadable, or under 「▸ 全部（157 列）」 (“▸ All (157 rows)”).
    • Width follows content, up to the layout width; when wider, it scrolls sideways inside .kit-table-scroll and does not break the layout.
    • Column names: function output and the data itself keep English names; summary tables the app builds itself may use Chinese; downloaded files keep the original column names.
    • Tables inside step cards have no outer frame and use a bg-stripe (pale) header row, not the black one.
  • Don’t: stretch to full page width; show hundreds of rows at once.

Chart

Charts sit in a white card, and each chart answers only one question; categorical colors use Okabe–Ito, taken in order. A plotly chart is always passed to kit_plotly_style() last, so it looks like part of the same app.

  • R:
    • Colors: kit_chart_colors() (categorical), kit_chart_neutral() (neutral), kit_chart_sequential() (color scale for continuous values).
    • Look: kit_plotly_style(p) (plotly is in Suggests; the app needs its own Imports: plotly); a downloaded single HTML file needs the app’s fonts: kit_plotly_fonts(p) (kit_plotly_style() already attaches them by default).
    • kitsUI’s kit_chart.R: kit_chart_categorical() (recolors charts drawn by kits with the categorical colors), kit_chart_role() (role colors).
  • Order when used with kits: kits’ plot() → kitsUI recoloring (kit_chart_categorical(), kit_chart_role()) → kit_plotly_style(). What kits draws is what you get; the app only applies colors and look.
    • Recoloring and kit_plotly_style() can be swapped: it does not touch colors set by kits or kitsUI.
    • The on-screen chart and the downloaded HTML use the same reactive (styled once), so both are identical.
    p <- plot(x$item, type = "category", items = shown)          # kits
p <- kit_chart_categorical(p)                                 # kitsUI
kitDesign::kit_plotly_style(p, filename = "item_category")    # last
  • Appearance (what kit_plotly_style() does):
    • Card: nb-card background, bw-frame frame, shadow-card (CSS .js-plotly-plot); the chart itself has a white background, and so does the downloaded PNG.
    • Text: all in the rounded typeface (sans), nb-ink; body 15px, legend and hover box 14px, tick labels 13px in text-hint.
    • Title: left-aligned, bold, about h5 (18px); wraps in the browser when the chart is too narrow. The kits subtitle (<sup>) stays on the next line.
    • Axes (every axis, including side-by-side panels): axis line nb-ink 1.5px, only left and bottom (no box on four sides), ticks pointing outward, grid lines line-soft, zero line line. With a single chart, the kits outer frame is removed; for side-by-side panels (category probability curves, Wright map) the outer frames become faint line rules, so the panels stay distinguishable.
    • Hover box: white background, nb-ink frame, rounded typeface.
    • Legend: no frame; with more than 4 items, or when the longest item is wider than 20 columns (a Chinese character counts as 2), it goes below the chart, horizontal, left-aligned; otherwise on the right. When the chart is narrower than 600px (phones) it always goes below. legend = "keep" leaves the position unchanged.
    • Color scale: heatmap-type traces switch to kit_chart_sequential() (very pale lime → bg-new → nb-green, darker for larger values; the minimum is not white, so 0% and empty no-data cells stay distinguishable); colorscale = FALSE keeps the original scale. Color bar text and frame follow the sizes and colors above.
    • Toolbar: no plotly logo; only “download as PNG”, zoom in, zoom out, and reset to the original range; in Traditional Chinese.
    • Margins: equally small on all sides; grows automatically when axes, legend, or color bar do not fit; axis titles and the legend are at least 16px from the card edge, so text is never cut off.
    • Left unchanged: data, axis ranges and ticks, specified colors, marker shapes, line widths and dashes, hover and legend text, chart height.
  • Palette:
    • Cohorts, scales, and scores take chart-blue, chart-orange, chart-green, chart-purple, chart-sky, chart-vermillion in order. plotly’s own default colors are replaced by the Okabe–Ito color in the same position.
    • Reference lines, bands, and unjudged points use chart-neutral.
    • Continuous values (pass rates and so on) use chart-sequential.
  • Rules:
    • The title above the chart states the question it answers.
    • Text on the chart follows kits’ original (English) and is not translated: the screen, the downloaded chart, and the chart from running kits in R are identical and can go straight into a paper. Labels the user typed (item IDs, domains, cohorts, waves, scale names) display as typed, Chinese included.
    • Below the chart, one hint line in Chinese explains how to read it; legend entries needed for a decision (for example Kept and Dropped in the linking chart) get their Chinese meaning in that line.
    • Leave at least 1.2rem between the chart and the explanation below it; the explanation must not overlap the x axis.
    • Download the chart with a secondary button (HTML via htmlwidgets::saveWidget(); the toolbar can also save a PNG).
  • Don’t: use plotly’s default colors or default toolbar; change plotly fonts and axis lines separately in the app; answer two questions in one chart.

Details row, advanced settings, settings summary (Details)

The details row holds the “details” in “results first, details later”: a row of collapsed small-text titles; the open one takes a full line.

  • R: kit_details_row(...) wraps a row of kit_detail(title, ..., open = FALSE); advanced options in the settings area use kit_advanced(..., title = "進階設定"); the one-line settings summary above results uses kit_settings_line(parts).
  • Appearance:
    • Titles are small text-hint text with ▸, no frame.
    • Opened content has no frame either; opened advanced settings get a faint line rule on the left.
  • You provide: a title for each detail (a noun: 「題目參數」 (“Item parameters”), 「這一回合的紀錄」 (“Log for this round”), 「用 R 怎麼做」 (“How to do it in R”)) and its content.
  • Rules:
    • Collapsed by default.
    • “用 R 怎麼做” (“How to do it in R”) is always the last item in the details row.
    • The settings summary goes above the primary button or the results, one line of small text: 「本回合 R1：M03、M36 · 參照世代 M03 · 沒有固定檔」 (“This round R1: M03, M36 · reference cohort M03 · no anchor file”).
  • Don’t: use accordion cards; stack frames inside details.

“How to do it in R” panel (CodePanel)

“用 R 怎麼做” (“How to do it in R”) turns the current settings into R code you can run as is, and always lives in the details row.

  • R: kitJoin’s kit_code_blocks(snips), kit_code_panel(output_id); kitsUI’s component of the same name.
  • Appearance:
    • Collapsed, it is one line of small text in the details row: 「▸ 用 R 怎麼做」.
    • Opened, from top to bottom:
      1. One line of explanation: 「以下程式碼依你目前的設定產生，是簡化的示範。」 (“The code below is generated from your current settings and is a simplified example.”)
      2. The version name (bold) and a 「複製」 (“Copy”) secondary button, on the same line.
      3. The code.
    • Only the code itself has a frame: bg-code background, bw-frame frame, no shadow, code size.
    • The code frame is at most the content width of the layout (inside the gutters) and must not break the layout when opened.
  • Rules:
    • When there are two versions (tidyverse, base R), the two “version name + code” pairs are stacked.
    • Ligatures are always off: <- and |> display as typed, so copying by hand does not introduce mistakes.
    • At most about 70 columns per line: for both code examples and explanations, letters, digits, and symbols count as 1 column, Chinese characters as 2. Break lines when writing templates; before display, kit_code() wraps automatically with kit_code_wrap() (after commas inside parentheses, and in comments at spaces or between Chinese characters; the parse result must be the same before and after wrapping), and kit_code_cols() counts columns per line; lines still too long after wrapping (unbreakable long strings) raise a warning (they do not stop).
    • Code that is still long scrolls sideways inside the frame and is not wrapped.
  • Don’t: open it by default; use cards, icons, or a green header; stack frames inside the frame.

Step card (StepCard)

Use step cards when a page has several steps in order: only one step is open at a time, and finished steps collapse to one line.

  • R: module kit_stepcards_ui()／kit_stepcards_server(id, titles, summaries, checks); low level kit_step_card(), kit_step_head(), kit_step_body() (steps 1–3 of kitJoin’s 「kits 作答檔」 (“kits response file”)). kit_steps() is the step list in the page guide, not a step card.
  • Three states:
    • Current step: white background, bw-frame frame, shadow-card; round number nb-lime.
    • Finished:
      • Collapsed to one line: round ✓ in nb-mint, followed by a one-sentence summary (for example 「5 個檔案 · 世代 TDCYP · 2009、2011（年）」 (“5 files · cohort TDCYP · 2009, 2011 (year)”)), and 「改」 (“Edit”) at the far right.
      • Frame border-disabled, no shadow.
    • Not yet available: border-disabled frame, text-disabled text, says 「先完成第 1 步」 (“Finish step 1 first”).
  • Rules:
    • Move forward only by clicking 「對，下一步」 (“Yes, next step”) (a regular button); go back to a finished step with 「改」 (“Edit”).
    • The primary button sits below all steps, only one; above it a 「還差：…」 (“Still needed: …”) line (see ReadyLine).
    • Tables in cards have no outer frame and a pale header row; on phones each row becomes a block (see FileTable).
    • The clickable area of 「改」 is at least 32px, with aria-label 「改第 N 步：標題」 (“Edit step N: title”); the current step gets aria-current="step".
  • Choose first, refine later: earlier steps ask only for the minimum choices (for example step 2 only picks “which columns are items”); detailed settings are edited later in a table (for example the item table in step 3 sets domain and scoring). The explanation in the earlier step must say 「之後在第 N 步還能改」 (“You can still change this in step N”), so users do not think everything must be set at once.
  • Tables to edit are open directly: when the lead of a step is a table to edit (for example the item table), show the table directly, not inside the details row; put a 「下載這張表」 (“Download this table”) secondary button next to it, so it can be downloaded at any time.
  • Don’t: open several steps at once; put cards inside cards.

Checklist

The checklist lists “things to decide” together with “things that are already fine”, placed before a conversion or a run.

  • Appearance: one item per row, with a mark on the left:
    • ! (text-decide): needs a decision. One bold sentence, one line of small text below saying why, and the decision buttons below that.
    • ✓ (nb-green): fine, or already decided. Weight 500; decisions the user made say 「（你選的）」 (“(your choice)”), with 「改回來」 (“Change back”) next to it.
    • i (text-hint): reminder, no decision needed.
    • Thin line-soft lines between rows.
  • Rules:
    • The recommended option goes first, and its button says 「（建議）」 (“(recommended)”).
    • A problem only counts as decided after a click (suspected missing-value codes, insufficient information); once decided, the result’s status box does not remind again.
    • List only what is needed; the per-item table goes under 「▸ 逐題看、逐題改（45 欄）」 (“▸ Review and edit item by item (45 columns)”), 25 rows per page, searchable.
    • Marks get aria-hidden="true", preceded by hidden text 「要決定：」 (“To decide:”), 「沒問題：」 (“OK:”), 「提醒：」 (“Note:”).
  • Don’t: list per-item reminders for hundreds of items.

Ready line (“what’s still needed”) (ReadyLine)

When the primary button cannot be clicked yet, one line above it says what is still needed and gives a link to fix it.

  • R: kit_ready_line(missing, link = NULL); in the server, kit_run_gate(session, output, missing, link) also disables the button; when there are not enough files, kit_need_files(n_files, need = 2L).
  • Appearance: one line of bold text-todo 「還差：…」 (“Still needed: …”), followed by an nb-green link 「到「檔案上傳」加入檔案 →」 (“Go to ‘File upload’ to add files →”); the disabled primary button is below.
  • Rules:
    • Show the primary button (disabled) from the start, so people know what they will click at the end of the page.
    • “Still needed” names the concrete thing and number: 「至少要 2 個波次的檔案，目前只有 1 個。」 (“Files from at least 2 waves are needed; there is only 1 now.”)
    • The server must still check; do not rely only on the disabled button.
  • Don’t: hide the button; repeat the same thing in a yellow callout.

Next step (NextStep)

“下一步” (“Next step”) sits at the bottom right of the page, appears only after results are out, and takes the user to the next tab.

  • R: kit_next_step(text = NULL, button_id = NULL, label = NULL, button = NULL).
  • Appearance: a hint sentence on the left (can be a list of destinations), and a primary button 「下一步：××× →」 (“Next step: ××× →”) on the right.
  • Rules:
    • When it appears: the status is 【完成】 (“Done”) or 【完成，但請注意】 (“Done, but note”).
    • Removed when results are outdated (【要重新執行】, “Run again”).
    • The button text names the next page.
  • Don’t: show it before results are out; place it in the middle of the page.

Diagram

A diagram uses a few small tables to show what the page does (before → after), placed below “這一頁做什麼” (“What this page does”).

  • R: kit_diagram(before, after, caption, arrow = "→"), with tables from kit_dg_table(df, title, added = NULL).
  • Appearance:
    • Supporting cast: no frame, tables as wide as their content, bw-hair grid lines, pale nb-page header row.
    • Values in the mono typeface.
    • Newly added columns have a bg-new background and 「（新）」 (“(new)”) after the column name, so color is not the only cue.
    • Empty cells say 「（空）」 (“(empty)”) in gray.
  • Rules:
    • Each small table has 2–3 rows and uses generic names (id, score, wave), not column names from a specific database.
    • One hint line of plain-language explanation below.
    • At ≤ 576px, “before” is on top, the arrow points down, and “after” is below.
  • Don’t: use real data; use the black header row of large data tables.

File table (FileTable)

The file table is the settings table in step cards or upload pages with “one row per file, one column per setting”; on phones each row becomes a block.

  • R: table.table.kit-file-table, with data-label (the column name) on each <td>; used in kitJoin’s upload page, step 1 of the kits response file, and kitsUI’s item bank selection table.
  • Appearance:
    • Desktop: a regular table; inside step cards, no outer frame and a pale header row.
    • ≤ 576px: the table and every row fill the card width; each row is a block, each cell preceded by a hint line with the column name, with line dividers between rows.
  • Rules:
    • Button positions are fixed in every row: unused 「上移」「下移」 (“Move up”, “Move down”) get invisible placeholders (btn invisible, aria-hidden), so buttons do not jump sideways.
    • Cells guessed from column names use bg-guess.
    • Inputs are at most the layout width.
  • Don’t: let the whole page scroll sideways on phones.

Page skeleton

Every tab follows this order from top to bottom (tabs with one primary button use kit_run_tab_ui()／kit_run_tab_server(), which handle the fixed parts and the state flow; the tab only writes its own settings, run, and results):

Header (one per app)
Step tabs (current is lime, finished get ✓, not yet available are gray)
What this page does: one sentence                         See steps ▸
Settings (left 1/3)          │ Settings summary and preview (right 2/3)
Advanced settings ▸
Still needed: … (while it cannot be clicked)
[ Primary button ]
Status box: [Done] one-sentence conclusion + at most 3 points
Key output: one table (with an h4 title) or one chart
▸ Detail 1   ▸ Detail 2   ▸ How to do it in R
                                       [ Next step: ××× → ]

State flow 

Not available ──(previous step done)──▶ Available ──(click primary button)──▶ Running
       ┌───────────────┬───────────────┬────────────┘
       ▼               ▼               ▼
    [Done]     [Done, but note]     [Stopped]
       └───────┬───────┘     (fix and click again, or click "Skip this round")
               ▼
   "Next step" button appears; tab gets ✓
(later changes to settings or files → [Run again]; the tab's ✓ is removed, later tabs turn gray)
  • After a run, scroll the status box to the top of the screen (no smooth scrolling when motion is reduced).
  • Show the first successful result by default; do not preselect one that stopped.
  • Actions that change results are clicked by the user; the button states the consequence clearly (「這一回合不做（題庫與連結不會改變）」, “Skip this round (item bank and linking will not change)”), and doing it leaves a log entry.

Phones (≤ 576px)

  • The page must never scroll sideways: document.documentElement.scrollWidth must equal the window width. Inputs and tables get max-width: 100%.
  • Tabs stay in one row and scroll sideways; do not wrap into several rows.
  • Tables in cards become “one row per block, column name on top” (data-label).
  • The header shrinks, so the first screen shows the page guide and the first setting.

Wording

  • Taiwanese Traditional Chinese, short sentences, conversational but not casual; one sentence says one thing. The subject is 「你」 (“you”) or omitted; never 「使用者」 (“the user”).
  • Conclusion first, then the reason: 「這一回合資訊不足，無法估計：每個人在要估的題只剩一題。」 (“Not enough information to estimate this round: each person has only one item left to estimate.”)
  • Numbers always carry units: 「688 人」 (“688 people”), 「3 個量尺」 (“3 scales”), 「2,058 欄」 (“2,058 columns”).
  • Buttons start with a verb and say clearly what will happen: 「開始校準」 (“Start calibration”), 「下載 CSV」 (“Download CSV”), 「到遺漏值處理頁改掉 →」 (“Fix it on the missing value page →”); never 「確定」 (“OK”) or 「送出」 (“Submit”).
  • Error messages always say what to do; R’s original message goes under 「▸ 原始訊息」 (“▸ Original message”).
  • The recommended option goes first, and its button says 「（建議）」 (“(recommended)”).
  • Word list (one word per concept):
Use this Not these
停下來 (stopped) 沒有完成、失敗、錯誤、中止 (not completed, failed, error, aborted)
要注意 (needs attention) 警告、warning
遺漏值 (missing value) 缺失值、missing
世代 (cohort) cohort (English may be added in details)
波次 (wave) wave (English may be added in details)
這一回合不做 (skip this round) 略過、排除、skip (skip, exclude)
  • Tab names are “noun + verb”: 檔案上傳 (file upload), 遺漏值處理 (missing value handling), 資料串接 (data join), 格式轉換 (format conversion).
  • Table column names: function output and the data itself keep English column names; summary tables the app builds itself may use Chinese; downloaded files always keep the original column names.

Accessibility checklist

Using it in a new Shiny app

New apps no longer copy files: just load the kitDesign package. The theme, styles (inst/www/*.css), browser-side scripts (inst/www/kit.js), and logo are all in the package, and every app uses the same copy.

# Install
remotes::install_github("jiewenTsai/kitDesign")

Add kitDesign to Imports: in the app package’s DESCRIPTION. Start the page like this:

library(kitDesign)

ver <- kit_app_description("kitJoin")   # reads the app's own Version, Date
ui <- kit_page(
  "KIT ×× 工具", "臺灣幼兒發展調查資料庫",  # "KIT ×× tool", "KIT database"
  tagline = "這個工具做什麼",              # "What this tool does"
  version = ver$version, date = ver$date,
  kit_navgroups(groups, "tabs"),          # or kit_flow_tabs(...)
  shiny::tabsetPanel(id = "tabs", type = "hidden", ...)
)

kit_page() already sets lang = "zh-Hant-TW", kit_theme(), the styles and scripts (use_kit()), and the header (kit_header()). When you build the page yourself with bslib::page_*(), add theme = kit_theme() and use_kit(). To start a brand-new app: kit_new_app(path, title, subtitle) (it includes the header, step tabs, an example tab written to the page skeleton, and tests).

Components come in three kinds:

  • Value objects (S3): kit_status (status box), kit_check／kit_checklist (checklist), kit_code (one version of code). They check their content when constructed (for example, the state can only be idle／success／warning／error／stale), render when placed directly in the page or passed to renderUI(), and print() shows a text version.
  • Modules (stateful components, *_ui(id) + *_server(id)): step tabs kit_step_tabs_*, step cards kit_stepcards_*, primary button + still needed kit_run_gate_*, How to do it in R kit_code_panel_*. One line per page; no state to manage yourself.
  • Markup functions: all other components, plus low-level versions of the two kinds above (older apps can switch over gradually).

Which function to use for each component:

Component Functions
Header Already included by kit_page(); on its own kit_header(), kit_app_meta(); version and date kit_app_description()
Step tabs (NavTabs) Module kit_step_tabs_ui(id, ..., groups = )／kit_step_tabs_server(id, states, tips); low level: kit_navgroups() + kit_navgroup(), kit_flow_tabs(aside = ), kit_tab_states(), kit_watch_tab_states()
Page guide (PageGuide) kit_tab_guide(), kit_steps()
Button kit_button(id, label, kind), kit_btn_class()
Download button (DownloadButton) kit_download_button(session, id, label, filename, content); tests kit_test_download()
Status box (StatusBox) Value objects kit_status(), kit_done_status(), kit_error_status(), kit_stale_status() (place directly in the page); low-level rendering kit_status_ui(); notifications kit_notify(); plain-language errors kit_abort()
Callout kit_callout(..., warn = ); cloud-version banner kit_cloud_banner(), usage notes kit_cloud_footer(), detection kit_is_cloud()
Data table (DataTable) kit_static_table(), kit_preview_table(), kit_rows_note(), kit_table_scroll(), kit_num(), kit_dims()
Chart kit_plotly_style() (look of plotly charts), kit_plotly_fonts(); colors kit_chart_colors(), kit_chart_neutral(), kit_chart_sequential()
Details row (Details) kit_details_row(), kit_detail(), kit_advanced(), kit_settings_line()
How to do it in R (CodePanel) Module kit_code_panel_ui()／kit_code_panel_server(); value object kit_code(code, label); wrapping kit_code_wrap(), line width kit_code_cols(); low level kit_code_panel(), kit_render_code_panel(), kit_code_blocks()
Step card (StepCard) Module kit_stepcards_ui()／kit_stepcards_server(id, titles, summaries, checks); low level kit_step_card(), kit_step_head(), kit_step_body()
Checklist Value objects kit_checklist(), kit_check(state, title, why, actions); single problems kit_problems()
Ready line (ReadyLine) Module kit_run_gate_ui()／kit_run_gate_server(id, missing, link); low level kit_ready_line(), kit_run_gate(), kit_need_files()
Next step (NextStep) kit_next_step(); link to another app kit_app_link()
Diagram kit_diagram(), kit_dg_table()
Scroll to results, open collapsibles, warn before leaving kit_scroll_to(), kit_open_details(), kit_unload_guard()
Page skeleton + state flow (RunTab) kit_run_tab_ui(id, run_label, guide, ...)／kit_run_tab_server(input, output, session, run_label, run, done, ...): still needed, settings summary, run, status box, notification, scrolling, run again, result details, How to do it in R
  • What every component looks like: kit_gallery().
  • The tool name stays “KIT ×× 工具” (“KIT ×× tool”); do not rename it when testing with other data (for example TDCYP).
  • The version line is always in the header and reads Version and Date from the app’s own DESCRIPTION (kit_app_description()), starting with the app’s package name (package =, e.g. “kitJoin v0.6.0 · 2026-10-31”); with show_kitdesign = TRUE the kitDesign version follows, so both versions are visible when reporting problems.
  • Versioning rules and release steps: release.md; old names in kitJoin and kitsUI: migration.md.
  • For new components or style changes, change kitDesign (inst/www/kit-design.css and R/); do not write separate CSS in the app. Use only this system’s tokens (colors, sp-*, type sizes), and check for an existing component before writing a new one.

Switching to another brand

kitDesign defaults to KIT (lime header, KIT green, bean logo). Projects other than KIT can use it too: change the logo and colors, and follow this design language for everything else (fonts, frames, shadows, spacing, components, wording rules). From kitDesign 0.3.0:

options(kitDesign.brand = kit_brand(
  "示範實驗室",          # "Demo lab"
  logo = "logo.svg",     # full logo for the header (SVG or PNG)
  mark = "mark.svg",     # browser tab icon (square; falls back to logo if missing)
  colors = list(accent = "#9cc0ff", primary = "#1f4fa3", page = "#f5f7fa")
))
  • Set it once and kit_page(), kit_header(), kit_theme(), kit_colors(), kit_chart_sequential(), and kit_plotly_style() all use it; for a single page use kit_page(..., brand = ).
  • The colors you can change are the ones with a --nb-* variable in the appendix below (see the note below the appendix “Color” table for the mapping); anything not given stays KIT. If only accent is given, accent_light is computed automatically (mixed with white); if only primary is given, primary_hover is computed automatically (darkened).
  • When changing colors, keep this document’s rules: text on color blocks is always ink, so ink on accent and on the four status colors needs 4.5:1; primary is link text and also needs 4.5:1 on page. Better not to change the four status colors; if you do, their meanings must not change.
  • Grays (text-hint, line, and so on), the focus outline, and the chart categorical colors (Okabe–Ito) do not change with the brand.
  • To see the result: kit_gallery(brand = "demo") (a blue demo brand).

Author’s decisions (2026-10-31)

  1. Tool name: stays “KIT”. TDCYP is only test data.
  2. Status labels: unified as 【完成】【完成，但請注意】【停下來】【要重新執行】 (“Done”, “Done, but note”, “Stopped”, “Run again”).
  3. Table column names: function output and the data itself keep English column names; summary tables the package builds itself may use Chinese; downloaded files keep the original column names.
  4. kitJoin tabs: three groups, unnumbered (準備 · 做出資料（選一個）· 其他工具; Prepare · Make the data (pick one) · Other tools).
  5. Table width: follows content, not stretched to the full page.
  6. Text on charts: follows kits’ original (English), not translated; labels typed by the user stay as typed (may be Chinese). The app only applies colors and kit_plotly_style().
  7. Danger button: salmon (nb-salmon), black text.
  8. Heatmap color scale: the minimum is a very pale lime, not white, so 0% and no-data cells are distinguishable.
  9. kits response file: step 2 only picks the item columns; domain and scoring are set in the item table in step 3; the default domain is the item group name with a trailing _, ., or - removed.

Where the code still differs

The sections above follow the code; check here when changing the code or the spec.

  • Recommended option: v0.2 proposed a mint-background button; the code never did it. Now it is only “goes first, text says (recommended)”.
  • Secondary button: section 9 of v0.2 proposed a 2px frame plus a 2px shadow; the code’s kit_button(kind = "secondary") is the small button (1.5px, no shadow, 0.85rem, weight 500). The white button with a shadow is only the default look of actionButton().
  • Type sizes: the spec has six sizes; inst/www/kit-brite.css still has values such as 0.85, 0.88, 0.9, 0.92, and 1.08rem, and the first line of the status box is 1.08rem.
  • Weight 500: the spec says only 400 and 700, but secondary buttons and “no problem” checklist items use 500.
  • Old grays: #4d4d4d, #6b6b6b, #9a9a9a, #c9c3b6 remain in some rules in inst/www/kit-brite.css (mostly overridden by later rules); the background of not-yet-available tabs is #ece8dc, not bg-disabled.

Appendix: tokens

In code, the CSS variable is -- plus the name, for example var(--nb-lime), var(--sp-3).

Color

Name Value Used for
nb-ink #141414 Ink: all text, 2px frame lines, hard shadows, the header background of the main data table. Text on color blocks always uses it.
nb-page #faf7f0 Paper: the whole page background (off-white). nb-ink on it is 17.2:1.
nb-card #ffffff Card: background of cards, inputs, tables, charts, and buttons (except the primary button).
nb-lime #c6d033 KIT lime, the lead color: header, primary button, current tab and step number, dropdown selection. Not a text color (only 1.57:1 on paper); put nb-ink on it (10.9:1).
nb-green #006835 KIT green (the same as the logo’s dark green): link text, progress bars, ✓ marks, selected checkboxes. 6.5:1 on paper, 6.9:1 on white. Not for large backgrounds or the primary button.
nb-green-hover #004d27 Link color on hover.
nb-sky #a8dcff Information: background of the sky-blue callout (kit_callout()), with nb-ink on it.
nb-yellow #ffde59 Needs attention: 【完成，但請注意】 and 【要重新執行】 status boxes, attention callouts, the cloud-version banner. nb-ink on it.
nb-salmon #ff9b8f Stopped: the 【停下來】 status box, danger buttons (delete, skip this round). nb-ink on it.
nb-mint #b9f0a8 Done: the 【完成】 status box, finished step numbers, the stripes of the upload progress bar. nb-ink on it.
text-hint #5a5a5a Supporting text: small hints, explanations, collapsible titles, group labels, secondary information in tables. 6.45:1 on paper, 6.9:1 on white.
text-disabled #6e6a60 Disabled text: not-yet-available step cards and tabs, disabled rows. 5.0:1 on paper.
text-todo #8a4a00 The “還差：…” (“Still needed: …”) line above the primary button, reminder text in per-item tables (bold). 6.4:1 on paper.
text-decide #a14a00 The ! mark for “needs a decision” in checklists. About 6.0:1 on white.
text-stop #8a2a00 Single problems in tables or lists (.kit-problems). 8.1:1 on paper.
line #d9d4c5 Faint line: the bottom edge of “What this page does”, the left rule of advanced settings, dividers in the phone file table. Lines only, never text.
line-soft #e3ded2 Faintest line: between checklist rows, top edge of the composite item ID block.
border-disabled #8a8a8a Disabled frames: not-yet-available or finished step cards, disabled buttons, not-yet-available tabs. 3.2:1 on paper (the threshold for frames and graphics is 3:1).
bg-disabled #e8e4d8 Background of disabled buttons (do not use opacity); not-yet-available tabs use the similar #ece8dc.
bg-stripe #f3f0e6 Zebra stripes in data tables; pale header row inside step cards.
bg-soft-hover #f1eee4 Background of secondary buttons on hover.
bg-code #fffdf5 Background of code frames (with a 2px nb-ink frame, no shadow).
bg-guess #fffbe6 Cells guessed from column names (pale yellow), reminding users to check them.
bg-new #e8f0a0 Newly added columns in diagrams (pale lime); not sky blue, which means “information”.
focus #0044ff Keyboard focus: 3px outline, offset 3px outward. Visible against black frames; 6.0:1 on paper.
logo-bean #aad05f Logo and illustrations only. Not for buttons or backgrounds (only 1.05:1 against lime).
logo-leaf #fff57f Logo and illustrations only. Not for any interface component (too close to the “needs attention” yellow).
chart-blue #0072b2 Chart categorical color 1 (Okabe–Ito): cohorts, scales, and scores take colors in order.
chart-orange #e69f00 Chart categorical color 2.
chart-green #009e73 Chart categorical color 3.
chart-purple #cc79a7 Chart categorical color 4.
chart-sky #56b4e9 Chart categorical color 5.
chart-vermillion #d55e00 Chart categorical color 6; beyond 6 categories, start over from the first.
chart-neutral #7f7f7f Neutral color for non-categorical elements in charts: reference lines, bands, unjudged points.
chart-sequential #f3f7d3 → #e8f0a0 → #006835 Color scale for continuous values (heatmaps, color bars): very pale lime (not white: white is reserved for no-data cells) → pale lime (bg-new, at 0.2) → KIT green (nb-green), interpolated in Lab space. kit_chart_sequential().

Colors a brand can change (kit_brand(colors = ) name → token → CSS variable): ink → nb-ink (--nb-ink), page → nb-page (--nb-page), card → nb-card (--nb-card), accent → nb-lime (--nb-lime), accent_light → bg-new (--nb-bg-new), primary → nb-green (--nb-green), primary_hover → nb-green-hover (--nb-green-hover), success → nb-mint, warning → nb-yellow, danger → nb-salmon, info → nb-sky (all -- plus the name). The values in the table are KIT’s; another brand replaces these, and chart-sequential is computed from accent_light and primary. Other tokens do not change with the brand.

Type sizes (base 17px)

Name Size Line height Weight Used for
display 1.75rem 1.25 700 Header h1 (tool name), one per app. Shrinks to 1.35rem on phones (≤ 576px).
h4 1.35rem 1.3 700 Section titles; 2.4rem above. Keep titles short; lists go in small text below.
h5 1.1rem 1.35 700 Subtitles, step card titles, the primary button, the first line of the status box (implemented as 1.08rem for the status box).
body 1rem 1.65 400 Body text, status box bullet points. The html base size is 17px, so 1rem = 17px.
small 0.95rem 1.4 400 Data tables (0.95rem), step summaries and checklist explanations (0.92rem).
hint 0.82rem 1.5 400 Small hints, collapsible titles, group labels, the version line, diagrams. The smallest size, about 14px; anything smaller is for chart tick labels only.
code 0.85rem 1.5 400 “How to do it in R”, raw error messages, values in diagrams. Ligatures always off; <- and |> display as typed.

Fonts: sans = “Chiron GoRound TC”, sans-serif; mono = “JetBrains Mono”, “Chiron GoRound TC”, Menlo, Consolas, monospace.

Spacing

Name Value Used for
sp-1 0.25rem Between an icon and its text. Spacing uses a 0.25rem unit.
sp-2 0.5rem Between components in one group, such as a row of buttons or between tabs (0.5–0.6rem).
sp-3 1rem Between components in one section, card padding, above the header.
sp-4 1.6rem Between tab groups, from “What this page does” to the first setting, above the details row.
sp-5 2.4rem Between sections (above h4), from the main content to “Next step”.
gutter 2rem Left and right page margins; 1rem at ≤ 768px.
content-max 1140px Content is at most 1140px wide, centered; wide screens get side margins instead of stretching to the window.

Corners

Name Value Used for
radius 8px All frames: cards, buttons, inputs, tabs, tables, charts, the header.
radius-bar 3px The upload progress bar only.
radius-round 50% The round step number in step cards (2rem square).

Shadows

Name Value Used for
shadow-header 4px 4px 0 0 #141414 The header only.
shadow-card 3px 3px 0 0 #141414 Results: status box, charts, the current step card, the primary button.
shadow-sm 2px 2px 0 0 #141414 Clickable things: tabs, regular buttons (actionButton default), dropdowns, focused inputs.
shadow-hover 1px 1px 0 0 #141414 Buttons and tabs on hover: move 1px down and to the right (2px for the primary button), leaving a 1px shadow; on press, move all the way with no shadow.

Frame widths

Name Value Used for
bw-frame 2px Frames of all top-level components: cards, buttons, inputs, tabs, table outer frames, code frames.
bw-line 1.5px Table row dividers, secondary button frames, the bottom edge of the explanation area.
bw-hair 1px Grid lines of diagram tables, the upload progress bar frame, between checklist rows.

Breakpoints

Name Value Used for
bp-phone 576px ≤ 576px: smaller header, file table rows become blocks, diagrams stack vertically, main actions take priority.
bp-tablet 768px ≤ 768px: 1rem side margins, tabs in one row that scrolls sideways, step card content not indented, settings and results stack vertically.
